correctness.rationale: For strict four-branch points the return map is affine, with M=A_R A_L^3 and Schur necessary conditions D=det(I-M)>0 and E=det(I+M)>0. The return fixed point gives x_1=(u+a+1)K/D, so x_1<0 forces K<0 since u+a+1>0 in the full saddle domain. Independently verified E=(u^2-2a)K-(1+ab)[u^2-(a+1)^2]-2a^2-2ab. Setting a=-r, v=-w, E decreases strictly in w>1+b. When K_b>0, the K=0 crossing has E*=-(1-rb)[u^2-(1-r)^2]+2r(b-r)<0; when K_b<=0, E_b(u) is decreasing for u>|1-r| and endpoint identities at 1-r, r-1, u_c=(r+1)(1-b)/(1+b) cover r<=1/r>=1 with the indicated b comparisons. All strict cases force E<0, contradiction. Exact symbolic identities and the two rational itinerary witnesses were recomputed; no finite parameter search replaces the all-parameter inequalities. Strict itinerary excludes switching points; unit-circle multipliers cannot yield asymptotic stability for a locally affine return.

value.rationale: It resolves a genuine structural distinction within the natural two-saddle mixed-determinant sector: an LLLR orbit exists but cannot be attracting under any admissible parameters, while LRRR can attract. It excludes an entire low-period stability window rather than merely repeating a local eigenvalue test; the uniform obstruction is useful in symbolic itinerary/bifurcation classification.

final_claim: For all delta_L<0<delta_R, tau_L>|1+delta_L| and tau_R<-|1+delta_R|, there is no locally asymptotically stable strict LLLR period-four orbit of the continuous two-piece border-collision normal form; the itinerary is feasible but unstable, while an attracting strict LRRR example exists.
